goal: Repair the highest risk local Tarot journey issues found in the reviewed audit, then verify the repaired flow on the connected Android device using synthetic customer scenarios.
successCriteria: A new Tarot session clears the previous result, question, selected cards, error, and progress so the draw screen starts at zero.
Journal Tarot entries retain the original question and card snapshot and can reopen a result view without starting a new reading.
Journal and Explore Tarot callbacks receive explicit stage values instead of press events, and invalid stage values cannot blank the flow.
The result identifies each card orientation, the share action is labelled as text sharing, and repeated saves do not create duplicate entries for one reading.
The mobile check passes and the repaired happy path is exercised on Q88549EEXCUOONGA with sanitized evidence and a customer-persona retest matrix.
untouchedSurfaces: Supabase credits, reporting endpoints, migrations, and backend contracts remain unchanged because the migration ledger is not an implementation gate for this local slice.
Tarot seed meanings, deck artwork, admin workspaces, authentication, payment entitlements, and public brand assets remain unchanged.
Customer QA governance and the previously reviewed Tarot audit remain unchanged; this plan only implements the approved local repair slice.

impact.entryPoint: Home, Explore, and Journal open Tarot through explicit stage callbacks; Start over and Back preserve the repaired flow state across topic, spread, deck, draw, result, and Journal reopen.
impact.dataWrite: The app writes only local Journal state and its existing sync payload; Tarot snapshots add question and deck context while preserving the existing card identifiers and orientation fields.
impact.backendContract: No endpoint shape changes are made; Journal sync receives the richer existing snapshot, and backend-down behavior remains the current local fallback.
impact.canonicalContract: TarotStage, JournalEntry, DrawnTarotCard, and the existing local Tarot result shape in apps/mobile/App.tsx remain the canonical client contracts for this slice.
impact.adminVisibility: No admin surface changes; any later operator report still receives only the existing sanitized event fields and no raw private question text.
impact.privacySafety: Reopen and share handling preserves the user-entered question locally but does not add it to the share payload; test scenarios use fictional questions and do not include account or journal data.
impact.observability: Existing Tarot open, draw, save, and sync events remain in place; no new telemetry is required, and device evidence records build, locale, route, and outcome separately.
impact.rollback: Revert the scoped App.tsx patch to restore the current local fallback; no migration or remote data change is required, and existing local entries remain readable by the prior summary path.
impact.surfacesIntentionallyUntouched: Credits and server reporting are intentionally deferred to a separate reviewed backend slice; deck content, assets, admin, and auth were reviewed and left untouched.
impact.agentHandoff: The delivery agent owns App.tsx only, uses synthetic customer scenarios and sanitized screenshots, runs mobile checks plus connected-device QA, and stops before backend or release actions.

canonicalContracts: docs/FEATURE_PRD.md defines Tarot result, Journal, and reflective safety expectations.
docs/CUSTOMER_PERSPECTIVE_QA.md defines synthetic customer scenarios, evidence fields, severity, and retest rules.
The existing TarotStage and JournalEntry client types in apps/mobile/App.tsx are the implementation contracts for this local repair.

sourceReview.reason: Reviewed Nilaza Tarot guardrails, target users, implementation boundaries, and manager workflow.
Reviewed mobile Tarot routing, source paths, and validation commands.
Applied the Whole-App impact, preflight, rollback, and manager acceptance requirements.
Reviewed Tarot reading, Journal persistence, and reflective safety expectations before implementation.
Reviewed the Tarot pilot scenarios and device evidence format used for the customer retest.
Re-reviewed the scoped App.tsx Tarot flow after the local repair patch; unrelated pre-existing changes remain preserved.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Read the current plan protocol and used its preflight, impact map, security review, device validation, and rollback requirements.

skillReview.name: nilaza-brand-experience
skillReview.evidence: Reviewed the Open Reflection identity and kept the repair within existing Tarot copy and visual surfaces.

skillReview.name: nilaza-tarot-content-qc
skillReview.evidence: Reviewed Tarot card meaning and orientation requirements; no canonical seed content is changed in this slice.

dependencyReview.evidence: The repair uses checked-out TypeScript and repository contracts only; connected-device validation does not require external product or policy claims.

securityReview.authzRls: No auth, authorization, RLS, or protected endpoint behavior changes are introduced.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Synthetic questions only; the original question is stored in the existing local Journal snapshot and is excluded from the share payload.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No credentials, tokens, or raw backend payloads are added to code, logs, or device evidence.
securityReview.externalInput: User question text remains untrusted display content; the patch does not execute it or send it to a new surface.
securityReview.dependencies: No dependency installation or generated runtime asset changes are required.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No migration repair, database push, release, deployment, or publishing action is planned.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if the mobile check fails, a private question appears in share output, the repaired device flow cannot be verified, or any backend/migration change becomes necessary.

workingTreeReview.note: App.tsx already contains unrelated uncommitted Nilaza work. The scoped Tarot repair will be limited to the callback, session reset, Journal snapshot/reopen, save dedupe, orientation, and share label changes described in this record; unrelated changes are preserved.

validationCommands: adb devices confirms the target Android phone is connected before the native test.
Connected-device Tarot customer QA: Home or Explore -> Tarot -> one-card draw -> result -> save once -> Journal reopen -> Start over -> new draw, with VI locale and sanitized screenshots.
managerTestPath: On the connected phone, open Tarot from Explore, complete a one-card synthetic reading, save it, open it from Journal, press Start over, and confirm the new draw shows 0/1 before any tap; then inspect orientation, share label, and the saved result. Review the agent matrix in docs/CUSTOMER_PERSPECTIVE_QA.md for retest coverage.
residualRisk: Native backend credit, reporting, network fallback messaging, and 78-card performance remain open findings for the next approved slice; this device pass covers the local Tarot journey only.
